summary: Defines a new MIKEY General Extension payload for carrying the key messages, reporting messages and parental control messages defined in the Open Mobile Alliance's BCAST Service and Content protection specification. This is an informational document that obsoletes RFC 4909.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 5410 defines how OMA BCAST messages fit inside the General Extension payload of MIKEY. It assigns a payload type and four subtype values, while leaving each message's detailed contents to the OMA specification.

subtitle: MIKEY fields for OMA BCAST key, reporting and parental-control messages.

tldr.problem: OMA BCAST defines several service-protection messages that need a defined place in the MIKEY message format.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC assigns MIKEY General Extension type 5 to OMA BCAST and defines four subtype numbers for long-term keys, short-term keys, reports and parental control.
tldr.outcome: RFC 5410 obsoletes RFC 4909 and is updated by RFC 6309. The payload must have integrity protection, and confidential data must be encrypted separately.

facts.label: Subtype values
facts.value: LTKM 1, STKM 2, LTKM Reporting 3, Parental Control 4

today: RFC 5410 obsoletes RFC 4909 and is updated by RFC 6309. It is an Informational RFC published in January 2009.

sections.title: Purpose of the MIKEY Extension
sections.content:
Multimedia Internet KEYing (MIKEY) has a General Extension payload so a message can carry extensions without allocating a new MIKEY payload type. The General Extension can appear in any MIKEY message and is part of the authenticated or signed data.

The Open Mobile Alliance (OMA) Broadcast (BCAST) group defines short-term key, long-term key, reporting and parental-control messages for service and content protection. RFC 5410 specifies how those messages use the MIKEY General Extension; their subtype-specific contents remain defined by the OMA specification.
sections.plainLanguage: MIKEY has a payload for extensions. This RFC assigns that payload to carry four kinds of OMA BCAST message.

sections.title: Type 5 and Its Four Subtypes
sections.content:
The OMA BCAST MIKEY General Extension uses type 5. Its data begins with an 8-bit subtype field followed by variable-length subtype-specific data.

The subtype values are 1 for a Long Term Key Message (LTKM), 2 for a Short Term Key Message (STKM), 3 for LTKM Reporting, and 4 for Parental Control. The RFC does not define the detailed format of those messages.
sections.plainLanguage: Type 5 marks a General Extension as an OMA BCAST message. Its next field identifies which of the four message types follows.

sections.title: Interoperability and Earlier Assignments
sections.content:
The RFC says OMA BCAST 1.0 compliance is the key interoperability question and leaves implementation testing to OMA test planning. The type assignment does not change MIKEY beyond RFCs 3830 and 4563.

RFC 5410 adds subtype values for LTKM Reporting and Parental Control, which were created after RFC 4909. It does not change the values already assigned by RFC 4909.
sections.plainLanguage: OMA's compliance testing checks whether implementations work together. This update adds two subtype values and leaves the earlier values unchanged.

sections.title: Integrity and Confidentiality
sections.content:
The OMA BCAST General Extension payload must be integrity protected. Keys and other data that need confidentiality must not appear in this payload in clear form; if such data is carried, it must be encrypted and encapsulated independently.

MIKEY's replay protection also covers the General Extension. IANA allocated type 5 and registered subtype values 1 through 4 for the OMA BCAST messages.
sections.plainLanguage: The extension must be protected against changes. Secret values need separate encryption because this payload does not provide confidentiality by itself.
